parts.name: body loop

physics.Basic_description: The main U-shaped body of the carabiner, appearing as a matte grey metallic rod bent into a loop.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the primary structural strength and attachment point for ropes or gear.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper can firmly grasp the straight spine or the curved bottom of the loop.
physics.reason: Small sports carabiners of this size are typically formed from solid aluminum rod or thick-walled tubing that approximates solid behavior for manipulation.

parts.description: The main U-shaped body of the carabiner, appearing as a matte grey metallic rod bent into a loop.
parts.function: Provides the primary structural strength and attachment point for ropes or gear.

parts.name: nose slot

physics.Basic_description: A small integrated notch or catch on the upper tip of the body loop, same grey metallic finish.
physics.Functional_description: Receives the gate key to secure the carabiner when closed.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and integrated to be grasped independently; part of the body grasp.
physics.reason: This is a machined or formed feature of the solid body rod.

parts.description: A small integrated notch or catch on the upper tip of the body loop, same grey metallic finish.
parts.function: Receives the gate key to secure the carabiner when closed.

parts.name: gate bar

physics.Basic_description: The straight movable bar that swings open, matching the grey metallic material of the body.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as the door to open and close the carabiner loop.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped to push open, though usually manipulated by pressing against the body.
physics.reason: Gate bars in small carabiners are typically solid pins or rods to withstand shear forces.

parts.description: The straight movable bar that swings open, matching the grey metallic material of the body.
parts.function: Acts as the door to open and close the carabiner loop.

parts.name: gate key

physics.Basic_description: A small protrusion on the end of the gate bar, same grey metallic finish.
physics.Functional_description: Fits into the nose slot to lock the gate in place.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small to grasp; interacts with the nose slot.
physics.reason: Integral solid feature of the gate bar.

parts.description: A small protrusion on the end of the gate bar, same grey metallic finish.
parts.function: Fits into the nose slot to lock the gate in place.

parts.name: hinge pin

physics.Basic_description: Small cylindrical pins at the hinge point, appearing slightly distinct or darker, likely steel.
physics.Functional_description: Pivot point allowing the gate to rotate open and closed.
physics.Grasped_description: Not graspable; too small and recessed.
physics.reason: Pins must be solid to support the rotational load.

parts.description: Small cylindrical pins at the hinge point, appearing slightly distinct or darker, likely steel.
parts.function: Pivot point allowing the gate to rotate open and closed.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
